3. The plaintiffs' case, in short, is that the suit property belonged to Masudjan and his father in law Nasruddin Choukider to the extent of 0.3333 acre and 0.6667 respectively. Nasruddin Choukider died before CS operation leaving behind two sons namely Sonamuddin (predecessor of defendant Nos. 1-9) Asanuddin (predecessor of defendant Nos. 10-13) and they equally inherited 0.26667 acre of land each. Nasruddin Choukider also left one daughter namely, Malancha who inherited 0.1333 acre of land. During CS operation the said Sonamuddin and Asanuddin got their names recorded in the CS Khatian excluding the name of Masudjan the daughter of Nasuruddin Choukider and the said record is incorrect and fraudulent. The plaintiffs are the heirs of Sonamuddin and they got 0.4666 acre of land and defendant Nos.1-9 are the heirs of Sonamuddin and they got 0.2667 acre of land and defendant. Nos. 10-13 are the heirs of Asanuddin. The suit property is ejmali property. The plaintiffs demanded partition on 27th Agrahayan, 1396 BS but the defendants refused. Hence the suit. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1 and 10 contested the suit by filing joint written statement stating, inter alia, that the suit property originally belonged to Sonamuddin and Asanuddin. Masudjan had no title and interest in the suit property but 0.3333 acre of land was wrongly recorded in the name of Masudjan and, as such, he executed a Nadabidecd in favour of Sonamuddin and Asanuddin. Subsequently 0.9 acre of land from khatian No. 9 was settled to Malancha Bibi which was ultimately recorded in the names of Somed Ali, Safed Ali and Wares Ali. The defendant Nos. 2 and 3 on 31-12-84 transferred their respective shares to Shahabuddin, son of defendant No. 1. The Government of Bangladesh subsequently acquisitioned some portion of the land from the suit land for the purpose of construction of Head Quarter Building of the then Rakhi Bahini but they have not been impleaded in this suit as party.
